regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Israel-Iran war stays kinetically frozen but has fully migrated into an economic and maritime contest: the 18 August talks deadline expired with no deal, the US opened an 'economic D-Day' sanctions campaign and re-designated Hezbollah an Iranian proxy on 20 August, and indirect diplomacy now centres on a single Iran-controlled Strait of Hormuz transit corridor via Oman and Pakistan.

Iran's proxy ring is the live front and is being used to impose costs without triggering direct war: Houthi ballistic-missile and drone strikes on Saudi tankers off Yanbu (24 August) and southern energy infrastructure, Iranian and Iraqi-militia drone attacks on KRG leadership in Erbil (14-17 August), and a Lebanon ceasefire collapsing around the 31 August disarmament deadline.

Israel is simultaneously escalating on three sub-state fronts — near-daily Gaza strikes (roughly 1,273+ Palestinians killed since the October 2025 truce) with creeping Yellow Line annexation, state-backed settler violence and mass displacement in the West Bank (HRW report 20 August; the IDF's own 'on the brink' warning 21 August), and strikes into Syria (Abu al-Duhur, 18-19 August) that risk a direct collision with Turkey.

Sunni jihadist violence is re-emerging as a secondary vector — the 22 August ISIS-suspected bombing of a Syrian security-forces bus near Damascus — while peripheral governance crises deepen (Tunisia protests into a second month over both repression and utility collapse; a Tripoli militia mobilisation). Regional maritime security is consolidating institutionally around the 13-nation Jeddah alliance, but Red Sea traffic remains roughly 60% down and war-risk premiums are climbing.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 23 Aug — Khan Younis: Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians, including a four-year-old child.
24 Aug — Bureij camp: Strikes on a house, mosque, water-desalination plant and warehouse killed at least seven, including two children.
25 Aug — Beit Lahiya: A strike on a home near Kamal Adwan Hospital killed three; a separate drone strike on civilians in al-Mawasi killed one.

26 Aug — Gaza City: Strikes on a mosque, desalination plant and displacement tents killed about seven; UN envoy Mladenov told the Security Council the near-daily strikes violate the Board of Peace disarmament plan.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The nominal October 2025 ceasefire persists in name only: near-daily Israeli 'imminent threat' strikes continue, the cumulative toll has passed roughly 1,273 Palestinians killed since the truce took effect, and Israel is incrementally hardening the Yellow Line — new concrete barriers on Salah al-Din Street and advances in Zeitoun and several other locations amount to creeping annexation of Gaza's eastern third. Board of Peace and Kushner-track pressure has not curbed the strike tempo and is unlikely to over the horizon. Expect continued high-casualty days coinciding with disarmament-implementation friction, throttled humanitarian access, and rising risk of a formal ceasefire collapse if a mass-casualty strike or an Israeli ground push past the line occurs.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 14-15 Aug — Ansar / Deir al-Zahrani: A Hezbollah drone wounded three IDF soldiers and Israeli retaliatory strikes killed 11, the deadliest exchange since the June truce.
26 Aug — Bayt es-Sayed: Israeli strikes hit the southern village, with smoke visible from Tyre.

31 Aug (deadline) — Beirut: The Lebanese Armed Forces are due to deliver the Hezbollah disarmament plan mandated by the 7 August cabinet decision; Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem publicly rejected any disarmament and dismissed the pilot-zone concept.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The June framework is functionally dead in all but name. Expect the 31 August LAF disarmament plan to be minimalist and rejected by Hezbollah, sustaining an Israeli strike campaign in the south and Bekaa plus periodic Hezbollah pinpricks. A wider flare-up is plausible if Israel strikes north of the Litani or hits a senior figure in Beirut, or if Hezbollah shifts from proxy attacks to acknowledged direct retaliation after further commander killings. Rome-track talks may continue in parallel but will not constrain kinetic activity.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 18 Aug — Washington: The 60-day US-Iran negotiating window expired with no deal and no talks scheduled; Trump said the US is 'low-keying' diplomacy.
20 Aug — Washington: The US imposed new sanctions on Hezbollah and re-designated it an Iranian proxy, with Trump renewing an 'economic D-Day' pressure threat.

25 Aug — Islamabad / Muscat: Pakistani mediation was reported as making 'significant progress'; Iran maintained its demand for formal control of a single Strait of Hormuz transit corridor via the Oman talks.
26 Aug — Tehran: Iran's armed forces designated BBC Persian, Iran International and Radio Farda a 'military target bank.'
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The kinetic phase stays frozen; the confrontation is now an economic and maritime war of attrition. Expect intensifying US sanctions, continued Iranian reliance on proxy escalation (Houthis, Iraqi militias) to impose costs, and slow indirect diplomacy via Islamabad and Muscat over a Hormuz transit corridor. A partial Hormuz arrangement is plausible but would be fragile. A return to direct strikes is possible if sanctions bite hard enough to threaten regime stability or if a proxy attack causes mass US or Saudi casualties.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 12 Aug — Bab al-Mandeb: A Houthi double-tap strike on a cargo vessel killed six crew and wounded ten.
20 Aug — Najran / Jazan, Saudi Arabia: The Houthis claimed simultaneous drone attacks on Najran Airport and the Aramco Jazan facility.
24 Aug — Red Sea off Yanbu: The Houthis fired a ballistic missile at the Saudi VLCC Amzan, saying the attack was 'in support of Iran.'
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Houthi blockade of Saudi-linked shipping and energy infrastructure is intensifying and is now broadening into the northern Red Sea toward Yanbu and the approaches to Jeddah. Saudi Arabia is signalling a possible naval or land offensive against the Houthi coast; a major Saudi ground operation, or a Houthi strike that kills Saudi personnel or sinks a tanker, would be the key escalation triggers. War-risk premiums and tanker rerouting will persist regardless, and coordination risk with Iraqi PMF factions against Saudi energy infrastructure remains.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 18 Aug — E1 corridor, east of Jerusalem: The government opened a construction tender for a project that threatens the displacement of 18-plus Bedouin communities.

20 Aug — West Bank: HRW reported Israeli-backed settler violence has displaced 107 communities (roughly 5,900 Palestinians) since 2023, with about 32,000 more people expelled by the military from Jenin, Tulkarem and Nur Shams since January 2025.
21 Aug — Tel Aviv: The IDF senior command formally warned the political leadership that the West Bank is 'on the brink' of violent escalation.
22 Aug — West Bank-wide: Israeli military raids and settler attacks injured at least 19 Palestinians.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Settler violence with direct or adjacent IDF participation continues to ratchet up, especially around Ramallah, Nablus and the southern Hebron hills, now compounded by the E1 construction tender and continued outpost growth. The IDF's own escalation warning signals that a trigger event — a settler-caused mass-casualty incident or a major Palestinian attack — could ignite a broader West Bank confrontation within the window. International condemnation is producing no observable policy change, and home requisitions and multi-day village sieges continue.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 14 Aug — Erbil: Three one-way attack drones were shot down by Global Coalition forces.
17 Aug — Erbil (Pirmam): Two Iranian drones struck the KRG prime minister's private office and the Parastin security chief's residence; no casualties, and Baghdad demanded an explanation from Tehran.

17-19 Aug — Dhi Qar: The Counter-Terrorism Service arrested a senior Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba intelligence officer; a judge dismissed the charges and he was released from PMF custody within two days.
25 Aug — Baghdad: The Operations Command convened on a regional security plan, following an 8 August Iraqi pledge to a Saudi intelligence delegation to stop attacks launched from Iraqi soil.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Direct Iranian drone strikes on KRG leadership targets in Erbil, plus militia-launched attacks toward Saudi Arabia, will continue while Baghdad remains demonstrably unable to disarm Kataib Hezbollah or Nujaba or to hold detained militia officers. Expect more Erbil strikes, sporadic ISF-ISIS clashes in the northern belts, and continued government hesitation between negotiation and 'decisive measures.' External pressure from Riyadh and Washington is growing; a militia strike that kills Gulf or US personnel is the main escalation risk.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 14 Aug — Jeddah: The 13-nation Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance formally launched, with Pakistan providing the deputy commander.
20 Aug — Najran / Jazan: Houthi drone attacks were claimed on the border region and the Aramco Jazan facility.
24 Aug — off Yanbu: A Houthi ballistic missile targeted the Saudi supertanker Amzan.
Through Aug — Red Sea: War-risk insurance coverage was extended roughly 800 km north to cover Jeddah and Yanbu.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Riyadh continues to absorb Houthi strikes on its southern border regions, energy sites and now Red Sea tankers off its west coast, while betting on the 13-nation Jeddah maritime alliance for political cover rather than unilateral escalation. The alliance offers limited near-term physical protection. A Saudi decision to launch a naval or land offensive against the Houthi coast, or a catastrophic strike on Yanbu or Jazan infrastructure, would be the pivotal 90-day development; continued Saudi participation in strikes against Iraqi PMF factions as forward deterrence is likely.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 18-19 Aug — Abu al-Duhur airbase, Idlib: Israeli airstrikes over a claim of Turkish military movement; the US assessed no basis for the claim and envoy Barrack said Israel may have been 'baiting' Turkey, as Israel and Turkey traded escalation warnings.

22 Aug — Damascus countryside (Maaroune–al-Tal road): An IED struck a bus carrying Internal Security Forces personnel, wounding several; ISIS is suspected, and Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Jordan condemned the attack.
22 Aug — Syria: An Israeli drone strike on a civilian vehicle caused injuries.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Two overlapping escalation tracks persist: ISIS-style attacks on the transitional government's security forces moving from the Badia into urban areas, and an Israel-Turkey collision risk over Syrian airspace and basing. Expect further Israeli strikes on sites linked to a Turkish deployment, continued Turkey-Syria strategic alignment, periodic jihadist bombings in Damascus and Homs, and growing US pressure on Netanyahu to de-escalate the Turkey dimension specifically; Turkey's push for an Interpol Red Notice against Netanyahu keeps the diplomatic breach open.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 7 Aug — Ain Sukhna / Suez: Tankers loading Saudi crude increasingly signalled Suez or Ain Sukhna to mask Red Sea origin.
14 Aug — Jeddah: Egypt remained a member of the Saudi-led Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance it joined after the 29 July Damietta drone strike.
Through Aug — Suez Canal: No security incident on Egyptian territory was recorded in the window; transits stayed roughly 60% below pre-crisis norms (about 275 a week), with a modest VLCC uptick.
countries.coa: Downgraded to HIGH from CRITICAL. No kinetic incident has struck Egyptian territory since the 29 July Damietta drone strike — more than four weeks — and current exposure is economic and maritime spillover rather than direct attack. Cairo stays embedded in the maritime alliance and pursues cautious Suez normalisation, but transit recovery is capped by the northern Red Sea threat and higher war-risk premiums, with continued revenue pressure on the state budget. The main risks are a Houthi strike in the northern Red Sea near Egyptian waters, a repeat of the Damietta-type drone incident, or a Sinai security deterioration; a second attack on Egyptian soil would be a significant negative inflection point for both the Canal and the alliance's credibility and would warrant immediate re-elevation.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 1 Aug — Amman: The US Embassy security alert citing heightened regional tensions and possible airspace closures remained in force; no new dated incident occurred in the window.
Through Aug — Jordanian airspace: Amman continued to serve as the overflight corridor for any Iran-Israel exchange, with no missile or drone activity recorded since 22 July.
countries.coa: Downgraded to HIGH from CRITICAL. Jordan is in a sustained kinetic lull — no Iranian strike or overflight-debris incident since 22 July, more than five weeks — and its current role is limited to an overflight corridor with standing precautionary alerts. The Jeddah alliance offers an institutional hedge for Aqaba specifically. A resumption of Iran-Israel strikes would immediately re-elevate Jordan to CRITICAL given its corridor position, and further use of Jordanian airspace as an interception zone carries associated civil-aviation risk; domestic protest risk over Gaza remains a secondary factor. The current calm should be read as contingent rather than durable.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 12 Jul — Gatrun, southern Libya: A self-proclaimed rebel group attacked an LNA checkpoint, remaining the most recent confirmed southern flashpoint.
13 Aug — Tripoli: Forces loyal to the Dbeibah government sent reinforcements into eastern Tripoli amid a militia buildup and renewed fears of clashes; no armed clash was confirmed in the window.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Tripoli stays in a calm-tension cycle; the militia mobilisation raises the odds of a short, sharp bout of intra-city fighting of the kind seen in 2023 and May 2026. The Gatrun area remains the last verified southern flashpoint. No national-level conflict is expected near-term; watch for a triggering assassination or checkpoint incident, alongside continuing political stalemate between the Dbeibah-led GNU and Haftar's LNA and periodic southern clashes linked to cross-border militia activity from Niger and Chad.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 21 Aug — Tunis: Hundreds to low-thousands marched for the second consecutive month demanding President Saied's ouster and the release of jailed opposition figures and journalists, citing water scarcity and power outages amid an extreme heat wave.
Ongoing — Nationwide: A prolonged heat wave drove record electricity demand, forcing utility rationing that also disrupted water pumping and compounded public anger.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Monthly large but so far non-violent protests are now an established pattern, amplified by summer utility rationing and economic contraction, and the security response remains arrests and media restrictions rather than lethal force. Escalation to sustained unrest is possible if a heat-related infrastructure failure, a high-profile death in custody, or new austerity measures land; Ennahda leadership remains detained without release, and sustained economic grievance could eventually produce a more volatile protest dynamic absent government action on the power and water crisis.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: The air war is escalating asymmetrically: Russia is exploiting Ukraine's near-total Patriot interceptor exhaustion (allied deliveries running at roughly a third of 2025 levels, with some launchers idle for weeks) with combined ballistic and Shahed barrages that increasingly hit civilian targets — the 21 August Kryvyi Rih shopping-mall double-tap killed at least 16 and wounded about 130.

Ukraine's deep-strike campaign is now materially degrading Russian fuel supply: Novokuibyshevsk, Salavat and the Lukoil NORSI refinery were all hit within one week (with reporting that 'all major Lukoil refineries are offline'), petrol is sold at under 30% of Russian stations, rationing covers 10-12+ regions, queues have reached Moscow, and MSC has suspended Novorossiysk container calls.

Ukraine's domestic political crisis is deepening: the NABU/SAP 'Forrest Gump' Energoatom corruption probe is now reported to reach into the Presidential Office, Fedorov's election demands and second-month protests continue, and Zelensky is reshuffling senior personnel heading into winter.

Diplomacy is active but stalled: the 24 August 'Coalition of the Willing' summit advanced funding pledges (Norway $9bn) but not a finished security-guarantee architecture, and a US-Russia backchannel is running (the CIA director visited Moscow, Kyiv was asked to pause strikes on the capital, and the Vatican held its first meeting with Lavrov since 2022) — with no ceasefire movement and Putin dismissive.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 21 Aug — Kryvyi Rih: A Russian double-tap Shahed strike on a shopping mall killed at least 16 and wounded about 130, including more than 20 children, with a second drone hitting rescuers.
25 Aug — Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast: A Russian FPV double-tap drone strike deliberately targeted rescue workers at the site of an earlier strike.

26 Aug — Nationwide: Combined Russian strikes killed four and injured about 95; the same day, NABU wiretaps in the Energoatom 'Forrest Gump' corruption case were reported to reach into the Presidential Office.

27 Aug — Zaporizhzhia / Odesa: An overnight ballistic-and-Shahed barrage injured at least seven, including three children, and damaged a school and residential buildings; Italy confirmed a package including SAMP/T and Aster 30.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, compounding. Expect the attritional air war to intensify into winter, with Russia sustaining massed ballistic and Shahed salvos against cities and the power grid while Ukraine's interceptor shortfall persists until SAMP/T resupply and possible joint Patriot production materialise — recurrent civilian mass-casualty events are likely. Ukraine will expand deep strikes on Russian refining, energy and logistics. The decisive variable is domestic: the NABU/SAP probe now touching the Presidential Office, Fedorov's election campaign and month-two protests could force further reshuffles and erode Zelensky's authority, though a wartime election remains improbable within the window. Coalition-of-the-Willing and US backchannel activity will keep generating frameworks without a ceasefire; Putin stays maximalist.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 19 Aug onward — Moscow and 10-plus regions: A 'second wave' of the fuel crisis saw Moscow petrol stations reimpose 30-litre limits and queues appear in the capital, with petrol available at fewer than three in ten stations nationwide and rationing or price controls across Krasnodar, Voronezh, Rostov, Ryazan, Tambov, Sochi, Crimea and Primorye.
22 Aug — Samara Oblast: Long-range Ukrainian drones (over 1,000 km) hit the Rosneft Novokuibyshevsk refinery and, for the first time, an Ozon e-commerce logistics hub.
23 Aug — Salavat, Bashkortostan: Ukraine struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refining and petrochemical complex, roughly 1,300 km from the border, causing a fire.

26 Aug — Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast: Ukraine hit the Lukoil NORSI refinery, Russia's second-largest gasoline producer, with reporting that all major Lukoil refineries were offline; a separate drone attack destroyed a warehouse in Tambov Oblast.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The nationwide fuel crisis is likely to deepen through autumn as Ukraine takes refining capacity offline faster than repair crews can restore it — expect wider regional rationing, informal price caps, extended diesel and gasoline export bans and sporadic local discontent, though the Kremlin retains the fiscal capacity to absorb the cost and will not soften its negotiating line (Putin's United Russia 'victory' framing). Black Sea export disruption, shipping and insurer withdrawal (MSC suspended Novorossiysk bookings on 27 August) and CPC tanker risk will pressure Russian and Kazakh crude flows and international oil prices. Retaliatory escalation against Ukrainian cities is near-certain, and continued spillover into NATO airspace over Romania, Poland and Moldova is likely.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 24 Aug — Minsk: Lukashenko said Belarus's 'capabilities have grown recently in relation to Russia' and that the two states 'stand on the front lines together,' while issuing an Independence Day message to Ukraine claiming future cooperation is possible.
Through Aug — Gomel region: Formation of the 37th Separate Air Assault Brigade about 40 km from the Ukrainian border continued, with a first battalion formed and a permanent base targeted for 2027.
Through Aug — Belarus-Lithuania border: Lithuania recorded 12 illegal-entry attempts via underground tunnels in 2026, with a third tunnel found near Varėna in recent weeks.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Window activity is continuity, not escalation: incremental militarisation near the Ukrainian border, sustained hybrid migration pressure on Lithuania and Latvia, and rhetorical alignment with Moscow alongside token Western-facing gestures. The 37th Air Assault Brigade will mature toward operational readiness through Q4, warranting monitoring for any shift from garrison to forward posture. Principal risks are a false-flag drone provocation in the Baltics, flagged by Lithuanian intelligence, and further border-tunnel and migration incidents; direct Belarusian combat entry remains low-probability.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: ~10 Aug — Moscow: Russian Deputy FM Galuzin warned that any 'armed provocations' against Transnistria would be treated as an attack on Russia, while assessing the risk as low.

Through Aug — Transnistria: Russia's simplified-citizenship decree continued to drive applications, with 200,000-300,000 residents already holding Russian passports and most of the remaining roughly 350,000 now eligible.
Aug — International press: The New York Times published a detailed investigation into Russia's large-scale hybrid operation against Moldova.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Expect continued Russian hybrid pressure — passportization, disinformation, energy leverage and rhetorical warnings against 'provocations' — with Moscow's passportization drive continuing to outpace its own deterrent measures and giving Russia a durable 'protection of citizens abroad' pretext regardless of price. Chișinău maintains its EU-accession-anchored reintegration track, with the Convergence Fund targeted for January 2027. Kinetic escalation risk stays low but non-trivial given Moscow's stated readiness to 'protect' Transnistria's Russian passport-holders.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 21 Aug — New York: UN Security Council members condemned Russia's continued occupation of Georgian territory on the anniversary of the 2008 war; de facto South Ossetia announced expanded crossing-point operations.
24 Aug — Tbilisi: Former PM Irakli Garibashvili was charged with bribery days after he publicly accused the government of 'setting a trap.'
26 Aug — Tbilisi: Bidzina Ivanishvili-linked companies were re-registered, with ownership shifted from Luxembourg entities to his wife's name — described by analysts as an 'offshore flight.'

Through Aug — Tbilisi: Daily Rustaveli protests passed roughly 630 consecutive days as the Anti-Corruption Bureau sent 'foreign agents' non-compliance notices to seven of eight leading NGOs, warning of criminal liability.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Georgian Dream continues authoritarian consolidation — NGO and media 'foreign agents' cases, selective detentions over Ivanishvili banners, and now criminal proceedings against former insiders that signal elite score-settling — while protests persist without dislodging the government. With 50-plus political prisoners already held, expect the crackdown to intensify and EU accession prospects to remain frozen (a visa-suspension review is due by March 2027). Watch for renewed unexplained blackouts from sabotage or infrastructure decay and additional restrictive legislation.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 21-23 Aug — Yerevan: The recall of Armenia's Ambassador to Russia was confirmed and framed as a deliberate signal to the Kremlin over unmanaged bilateral tensions.

~24 Aug — Yerevan: Pashinyan said Armenia will not return to the CSTO and 'would welcome' being expelled, while Yerevan prepares a formal EU membership application; the Kremlin said Armenia is 'free to leave.'
Through Aug — Yerevan: Armenia continued to withhold its CSTO budget contribution for a 12th month; exports to the EU rose about 80% year-on-year in the first half of 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Yerevan-Moscow rupture is widening — ambassadorial recall, open CSTO-exit talk, EU-application preparation and rising trade friction — but Armenia's exposure via Russian gas, nuclear fuel, remittances, roughly $12bn in bilateral trade and the 102nd base points to a managed decoupling rather than a clean break. Expect Moscow to respond with coercive measures through energy, border and FSB leverage, expanded trade bans and disinformation rather than conciliation; US-brokered normalisation with Azerbaijan and the TRIPP corridor track further reduce Armenian dependence on Moscow.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 5-18 Aug — Ukraine: Fallout continued from Russian strikes on SOCAR and Azeri-linked energy assets, with Baku-Moscow relations described as being in 'freefall.'
~18 Aug — Moscow: Russian MFA spokeswoman Zakharova pledged to 'protect' Sputnik Azerbaijan journalists after Baku placed them on an international wanted list.
~24 Aug — Baku: Azerbaijan's foreign ministry raised 'provocative, insulting and threatening' statements in Russian media through diplomatic channels, demanding 'concrete steps' from Moscow.
25-27 Aug — Lachin: Azerbaijan held the inaugural Lachin International Film Festival in reclaimed Karabakh as soft-power signalling.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Baku-Moscow ties stay cold: expect further diplomatic notes over hostile Russian media, sharp reaction to any new strike on SOCAR or Azeri-linked assets in Ukraine, a sustained crackdown on Kremlin-linked media mirrored by domestic press repression (the Toplum TV sentences), and continued drift from Russian-aligned bodies, with a realistic chance Baku moves toward a formal Council of Europe withdrawal decision within 90 days. Azerbaijan deepens alignment with Ukraine, Türkiye, the US and the EU. Open Russia-Azerbaijan conflict is unlikely; episodic friction and escalation are likely.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Jihadist consolidation in the west is deepening while inter-factional war spreads: JNIM is tightening the economic siege of Bamako into its roughly 12th month with Kayes and Nioro du Sahel sealed, and the JNIM-ISSP war is escalating across the Liptako-Gourma tri-border after JNIM killed ISSP's northeastern-Burkina emir on 17 August — inter-factional violence is now bleeding into Niger and Nigeria.

Sudan's war is externalising: the El Obeid siege is deepening toward a possible El-Fasher-style mass-atrocity event (20 August village raids killed six and displaced over a thousand; power and water infrastructure is collapsing; cholera is spreading), 200,000-plus people have been newly displaced across Kordofan, and — for the first time — Chad has attributed a strike more than 100 km inside its territory to the Sudanese state rather than the RSF.

External-partner realignment is diverging: Chad has publicly confirmed rebuilding military cooperation with France (troops back since April, providing air support and ISR) even as Mali's dependence on Russia's Africa Corps keeps yielding little against JNIM and generating atrocity allegations that harden the insurgency's narrative.

Mass-abduction and migration pressures are rising together: Lakurawa's 21-22 August mosque raid in Niger State marks its deepest reach into central Nigeria, Borno's 78 abducted schoolchildren remain held after roughly 100 days, and the Atlantic migrant route is accelerating (300-plus rescued off Mauritania on 21 August) ahead of the September-November peak season.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 13 Aug — Kidal / Gao: The Azawad Liberation Front released 82 captured Malian soldiers, with six more freed 'in poor health' and transferred on 16 August.
17 Aug — Diallassagou, Mopti region: A JNIM ambush on a FAMa position killed around 15 soldiers.
20 Aug — Bombori, Mopti region: HRW disclosed that Russian Africa Corps personnel summarily killed nine civilians, including four children, on 10 July.

20-27 Aug — Kayes / Nioro du Sahel axis: The JNIM blockade continued into its roughly 12th month, with both cities sealed and Bamako resupplied only by military-escorted fuel convoys; more than 300 tankers have been destroyed since September 2025.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The fuel siege is structural and FAMa has shown no capability to break it; expect sustained convoy ambushes on the Kayes, Nioro and Mopti-Ségou corridors, recurring fuel rationing and price spikes in Bamako, and continued Africa Corps attrition without operational effect. Further HRW and UN documentation of extrajudicial killings will harden JNIM's narrative and accelerate recruitment, and episodic JNIM/FLA action close to Bamako remains plausible. Watch for JNIM escalating the economic blockade toward a declared full siege and for aviation-fuel scarcity degrading FAMa air support; there is no meaningful loosening of the blockade in prospect absent a negotiated deal or major military breakthrough.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 14 Aug — Niger: Islamic State Sahel Province released a kidnapped US missionary after US-brokered diplomacy.

15 Aug — Séguédine, Kawar region: The Toubou rebel group MPLJ attacked security positions, killing several personnel and abducting three — a re-emerging third front along the Djado gold and Libya route.

20-27 Aug — Nationwide: No independently verified major FAMa or civilian mass-casualty incident was located for the window; the disputed 15 August air-strike claim on Boko Haram figure 'Bakura' remains unconfirmed.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Two-front pressure persists — JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province in Tillabéri, ISWAP and Boko Haram in Diffa — now compounded by renewed Toubou insurgent activity around Kawar. The junta remains isolationist and outside the MNJTF, with limited partner support, so expect continued garrison ambushes, IEDs and kidnappings and a standing urban-attack risk in Niamey. Thinner reporting this week reflects junta information restrictions and a lull rather than resolution; further mass-casualty incidents are likely within 90 days, and continued cross-border coordination with Nigerian and Chadian forces will be needed to prevent renewed large-scale ambushes in Tillabéri.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 3 Aug — Youba village, North region: JNIM fighters killed 14 civilians, including four children, to punish the community for defying the group's ban on cultivating tall crops.
17 Aug — Northeastern Burkina Faso: A JNIM ambush killed ISSP's emir for the northeast and several fighters, with pro-JNIM channels warning ISSP is preparing a large-scale retaliatory offensive.
Late Aug — Liptako-Gourma: ACLED assessed the 17 August killing as a potential catalyst for a new phase of the JNIM-ISSP war along the Niger frontier.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; the open JNIM-ISSP conflict is the key deteriorating vector. It could cut two ways over the next 90 days: it may temporarily divert both groups' capacity from state and civilian targets as they contest territory in the northeast, but a decisive ISSP counter-offensive risks a fresh spike in civilian massacres as both sides punish communities suspected of aiding the rival faction. JNIM retains the initiative across the North, Sahel, Est and Boucle du Mouhoun, besieging provincial towns like Djibo and continuing punitive killings; junta VDP mobilisation will drive further abuses.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: Mid-Aug — Umm Arda (about 20 km SW of El Obeid): An attack blamed on the RSF killed roughly 18, wounded 17 and displaced more than 300 families.
20 Aug — Um Dareisa and Al-Shaqla villages (about 40 km SW of El Obeid): An RSF raid killed six civilians and forced more than 1,000 people from 215 families to flee on foot to El Obeid.

20 Aug — El Obeid: The IOM warned of 200,000-plus newly displaced across Kordofan since late 2025; the city's main power transformer was destroyed by drone strikes, hitting water pumping and hospitals amid a worsening cholera outbreak.
25-26 Aug — Qardud and Abu Hamama, South Kordofan: SPLM-N (al-Hilu) attacks on the Otoro community killed 27, including four children, driving mass displacement toward Kadugli.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, escalating. El Obeid is the clearest bellwether for whether North Kordofan replicates the El-Fasher pattern of siege-to-massacre: continued RSF ground probes from the southwest, drone strikes on power and water infrastructure, and village-clearance raids funnelling displaced civilians into an already water-stressed, cholera-affected city point toward a tightening noose, and UN warnings of 'risk of mass atrocities' should be read as an early-warning indicator. Absent a ceasefire or a decisive SAF counter-offensive, expect further reprisal-style raids, rising civilian casualties and accelerating displacement straining Chad's border reception capacity; SPLM-N ethnic violence in South Kordofan is a secondary escalation with its own displacement dynamic.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 2 Aug — Ghara al-Zawiya, North Darfur near the Chad border: An RSF drone strike reportedly caused dozens of casualties, part of a broader pattern of RSF drone activity spilling into Chadian territory.
19 Aug — N'Djamena: Chad publicly confirmed the rebuilding of military cooperation with France, with French troops back since April for training, intelligence and air support.

22-23 Aug — Ennedi Est region (more than 100 km inside Chad): Chad's General Staff accused the Sudanese armed forces — not the RSF — of drone and air strikes on a vehicle convoy, placed all military units on nationwide high alert and warned belligerents against spillover.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. The first acknowledged strike by Sudanese state forces more than 100 km inside Chadian territory, together with a nationwide military alert, marks a qualitative shift from contained border spillover to direct interstate-escalation risk. Expect further cross-border incidents in Ennedi, Wadi Fira and Ouaddaï, a possible Chadian shift in air-defence posture or retaliatory strikes into Sudan, and continued refugee inflow toward the roughly one million Sudanese already sheltering in the east. French ISR and air support will expand, and the probability of a miscalculation drawing Chad directly into the war is now non-trivial; any major escalation of the El Obeid siege would likely trigger a fresh refugee surge into eastern Chad.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 21 Aug — off Nouadhibou: The coastguard rescued more than 300 migrants, including 40 children, from an overloaded pirogue that had left The Gambia carrying 315 people.
22-23 Aug — off Nouadhibou: Coastguards rescued a further roughly 42 migrants from a separate boat that suffered engine failure.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Migrant departure volumes along the Atlantic route show no sign of abating heading into the September-November peak season, and the past week's back-to-back rescue of over 340 people indicates coastguard capacity is being stretched by sustained, high-density departures from The Gambia and Senegal. Expect continued high-frequency rescue operations interspersed with periodic further fatal shipwrecks off Nouadhibou and Dakhla given persistent use of overloaded, under-fuelled pirogues; direct security risk to foreigners stays low, with exposure primarily humanitarian and consular, and the 90-day outlook points toward Mauritania's highest annual migrant-transit and fatality figures on the Atlantic route to date.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: ~18 Aug — Tsafe LGA, Zamfara: Security forces killed 17 bandits after an attack on motorists on the Gusau-Funtua highway.
19 Aug — Gidan Bawa, Bakori LGA, Katsina: Army, DSS and Community Watch Corps foiled a planned mass abduction and killed around 24 bandits.
21 Aug — Maiduguri, Borno: Families of the 78 schoolchildren seized in Askira/Uba LGA protested at roughly 100 days in captivity, with UNICEF renewing its call for their release.

21-22 Aug — Borgu LGA, Niger State: Lakurawa fighters raided four villages and stormed Kpenya mosque during Friday prayers; residents reported more than 60 worshippers abducted, and President Tinubu ordered a military rescue operation.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The north-western kidnap economy across Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi and Niger states will sustain mass abductions despite tactical security wins. Lakurawa's expansion from the Sokoto and Kebbi borderlands into Niger State — blending banditry with ISSP-aligned jihadism, and now fighting the rival Mahmuda faction — opens a new front toward Kwara and Benin, reminiscent of JNIM/ISSP's Sahel tri-border expansion. Expect continued high-frequency abduction-for-ransom incidents and highway ambushes with slow force response, while the unresolved captivity of the 78 Borno schoolchildren becomes a growing political liability for Abuja.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: The US carrier gap is the defining variable: the USS George Washington strike group left the Indo-Pacific in mid-August for the Middle East, removing the only forward-deployed US carrier, and China moved immediately to exploit it — bomber and amphibious drills at Scarborough Shoal, sustained coast-guard pressure at Pag-asa, and PLAN warships openly shadowing the 19-25 August Philippine-US-Australia maritime activity — with allied navies partially backfilling through minilateral patrols.

China-Russia-North Korea alignment is now stated openly: Japan's 2026 Defense White Paper frames the three as coordinating, North Korea timed missile barrages on 12 and 20 August to the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise while declaring its nuclear status 'irreversible,' and Wang Yi's Seoul visit pushed synchronised messaging against US alliance activity.

Air power and drones are substituting for ground control in internal conflicts: Myanmar's junta drove August civilian deaths past 100 with airstrikes on villages, IDP sites and a Sagaing monastery (21 August, 14 killed), and Indonesia shifted to repeated drone strikes on TPNPB positions in the Papua highlands (16-20 August) — both generating UN and rights-body scrutiny.

Sub-state violence is persistent across South and Southeast Asia: the BLA's tempo remains high and is spreading into northern, Pashtun-majority Balochistan (Pishin laborer killings, 24 August), Manipur ethnic violence reignited (arson 17 August, protest 20 August, Kamjong attack 23 August), Sri Lanka's prison system stays in crisis, and electoral and constitutional friction adds instability in Azad Kashmir and Bangladesh.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 12 Aug — Sea of Japan: North Korea fired a ballistic missile roughly 690 km, its ninth launch of 2026, days before the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise opened.
18-19 Aug — Pyongyang: State messaging reaffirmed that nuclear-weapons status is 'irreversible and permanent' and set the exclusion of denuclearization as a precondition for any Trump-Kim summit.
20 Aug — Pyongyang area: A barrage of about 10 short-range ballistic missiles was fired toward the East Sea as Ulchi Freedom Shield wound down and hours after Trump floated a new Kim summit.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect a continued missile-testing cadence timed to any US-ROK exercise or high-level diplomacy, plus a possible satellite or longer-range test around the APEC window and Trump's planned November Asia trip, while Pyongyang keeps dangling and deferring a summit to extract sanctions and recognition concessions and deepens the Russia relationship. Kimsuky and allied RGB units will likely intensify AI-enabled spear-phishing against South Korean, Japanese and US-aligned targets. Kinetic escalation remains low-probability; the most dangerous scenario is a lethal grey-zone incident at the maritime boundary, and a seventh nuclear test remains a possible negotiating shock.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 11 Aug — Geneva: The UN's IIMM reported a documented escalation of deliberate air attacks on civilians, including use of paramotors and gyrocopters.
21 Aug — Swel Le Oh village, Myaung Township, Sagaing: A junta fighter jet bombed a monastery during a meditation retreat, killing 14 and wounding about 20.
24 Aug — Thandwe Township, Rakhine State: An airstrike killed about 14 civilians, pushing the township's monthly toll to roughly 19 killed and 40 injured.
2-24 Aug — Rakhine and Chin States: Sustained airstrikes on Arakan Army-held areas pushed August civilian deaths past 100.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, deteriorating. With the monsoon limiting ground movement and the post-election 'legitimacy' narrative demanding activity, the junta will lean further on indiscriminate air power — jets, attack helicopters and cheap motorised aircraft — against Rakhine, Sagaing, Chin and northern Shan, producing continued mass-casualty strikes on villages, monasteries and IDP camps and worsening displacement and aid access. Expect further UN and IIMM documentation of deliberate civilian targeting, continued Arakan Army consolidation in Rakhine, and a risk of junta strikes spilling toward the Bangladesh border and Chinese-interest infrastructure at Kyaukphyu; no credible ceasefire path exists in this window.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 10 Aug — AJK: The reduced third phase of the Azad Kashmir election was held amid JAAC-led unrest and a boycott; PML-N emerged the largest bloc.
21 Aug — Khadkocha, Mastung, Balochistan: A roadside blast killed four workers.
24 Aug — Saranan / Pishin, Balochistan: A BLA attack killed five Punjabi road-construction laborers, pushing insurgent violence into northern, Pashtun-majority Balochistan.
25-27 Aug — KP and Balochistan: The military reported 11 militants killed in intelligence-based operations, following 49 killed in multi-district operations days earlier.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The BLA and BLF will maintain a high operational tempo — laborer killings, convoy IEDs, complex 'Majeed Brigade' attacks and highway blockades — with a notable geographic spread from the Baloch core into Pishin and Killa Abdullah and along the coastal CPEC axis. Expect continued army and Frontier Corps clearance operations, drone strikes and elevated civilian-security casualties, plus periodic TTP attacks in KP and cross-border friction with Afghanistan. AJK post-election grievances over the reserved seats and electoral reform remain a live unrest driver in Muzaffarabad; Islamabad's posture is kinetic suppression over political accommodation.

countries.name: India
incidents: 17 Aug — Kangpokpi and Senapati districts, Manipur: Pre-dawn arson hit Kuki and Naga villages; a CRPF trooper was injured in a subsequent gunfight and NH-2 was blocked by protests.
20 Aug — Namdilong, Imphal West: A protest over six Naga civilians abducted and killed from Leilon Vaiphei turned violent; security forces used tear gas, injuring about seven.
23 Aug — Kamjong district, Manipur: Suspected militants shot dead two people and burned houses, prompting a Naga armed group to declare a shutdown.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained (watch). Renewed arson and targeted killings after months of relative calm have not yet returned Manipur to 2023-scale violence, but the state under President's Rule stays volatile along the Meitei-Kuki-Zo and now Meitei-Naga fault lines. Expect further arson, ambushes, highway blockades and communal shutdowns, with flashpoints around the Naga-civilian-killings investigation and any delimitation or electoral-roll moves; security-force use of tear gas on protesters is itself an escalation vector, and there is added north-east risk from Myanmar spillover. Nationally MODERATE holds; localised CRITICAL conditions persist in the Manipur hill districts.

countries.name: China
incidents: 1-3 Aug — Scarborough Shoal: The PLA Navy surged an amphibious group and maritime-strike bombers for drills roughly 120 nautical miles off Luzon.
15-16 Aug — Western Pacific: The USS George Washington carrier strike group departed the Indo-Pacific for the Middle East, leaving no forward-deployed US carrier in theater.
19-20 Aug — Seoul: FM Wang Yi made his first standalone South Korea visit since 2021, coordinating peninsula messaging and pressing back on US alliance activity.
26 Aug — West Philippine Sea: PLAN warships shadowed a Philippine-US-Australia multilateral maritime activity.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Beijing will exploit the US carrier gap with intensified but calibrated coercion — coast-guard and maritime-militia massing and water-cannon use at Scarborough and Pag-asa, near-daily Senkaku patrols, and combined-arms activity east of Taiwan increasingly with third-country participation — alongside coordinated diplomatic pressure on Japan reinforced by China-Russia messaging. PLA sortie and vessel counts near Taiwan will likely stay elevated but below crisis thresholds, with the risk of a collision or injury incident at Scarborough or Second Thomas Shoal elevated; a major PLA exercise around Taiwan is plausible if Taipei or Washington takes a step Beijing deems provocative.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 2 Aug — Taiwan: The Han Kuang 42 exercise concluded, debuting M1A2T Abrams tanks and a new Littoral Combat Command; Beijing dismissed it as a 'wasteful charade.'
10-21 Aug — Taiwan: The US Coast Guard conducted small-craft and maritime-patrol training with Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration under the 2021 working-group MOU.
13 Aug — Taiwan Strait: The defense ministry detected 18 PLA aircraft plus 11 PLAN and three official ships around Taiwan.
24 Aug — Taipei: Prosecutors indicted an Nvidia manager and eight others for smuggling 74 servers of AI chips to China via Japan and Indonesia — the island's first such crackdown.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. PLA air and naval presence stays at the 'new normal' baseline with episodic surges tied to political triggers such as US arms notifications, transit diplomacy or legislative moves. The AI-chip smuggling probe will widen — more indictments, tighter export-control enforcement and friction with firms operating cross-strait — while deepening US-Taiwan coast guard cooperation and Taiwan's force modernisation continue. Watch the east-coast Pacific approaches, where China is normalising operations, and undersea-cable interference near Matsu and Penghu.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 11 Aug — Manila: Defense Secretary Teodoro called China's Pag-asa conduct 'irresponsible, escalatory and provocative' after a former Chinese diplomat said Thitu 'will be taken over.'

11-17 Aug — West Philippine Sea: The AFP logged 23 Chinese vessels (20 coast guard, three PLAN) at three features, including helicopter reconnaissance off Pag-asa; local fishermen reported encirclement.
19-25 Aug — Philippine EEZ: The 10th Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity of 2026 was held with the US and Australia.
26 Aug — West Philippine Sea: PLAN warships shadowed that multilateral activity.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, aggravated by the US carrier gap. With no US carrier in theater, expect China to test Philippine resolve at Pag-asa and Scarborough — coast-guard blocking and shadowing, water cannon, possible landings on nearby unoccupied features, and pressure on Pag-asa resupply and the new coast guard outpost. Manila will respond with more frequent multilateral patrols with the US, Australia and Japan, its transparency-initiative publicity, and hardening of Kalayaan features. There is a high risk of a ramming, water-cannon injury or blockade standoff that triggers Mutual Defense Treaty consultation debate, and domestic pressure for a firmer line will grow.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: Ongoing — Seoul: The foreign ministry confirmed intruders had access to the Korea National Diplomatic Academy from April 2025 to early February 2026, exposing up to roughly 10,000 records covering nearly all serving diplomats.
19-20 Aug — Seoul: Wang Yi met FM Cho Hyun, with North Korea and the alliance drills on the agenda.
20 Aug — Seoul: The Joint Chiefs tracked and condemned the North Korean SRBM barrage timed to the close of Ulchi Freedom Shield.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Diplomatic Academy breach's true duration and scale are worse than first reported but this is a continuation of a known incident, not a new escalation. Fallout will drive a government-wide credential reset, audits of contractor-run IT and e-learning systems, and likely additional disclosures of DPRK-linked intrusions into the foreign ministry, defense and think tanks. Kimsuky activity will continue with AI-assisted lures; on the military track, expect episodic DPRK launches around any exercise or Trump-Kim signalling and GPS jamming affecting civil aviation and shipping near the NLL. The Lee government maintains an engagement posture but has little room to reciprocate.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 11 Aug — Canberra: A To Lam-Albanese summit upgraded defense cooperation and signed a critical-minerals and semiconductor supply-chain pact, an explicit hedge against China.
16 Aug — South China Sea: China's unilateral fishing moratorium expired and Vietnamese vessels resumed operations in contested waters, raising coast-guard-encounter risk.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Hanoi continues its 'bamboo diplomacy' — deepening ties with Australia, the US, Japan, the Philippines and the EU while managing Beijing carefully and avoiding public confrontation. Expect continued Spratly outpost dredging and construction, periodic low-key coast-guard standoffs near Vanguard Bank and around resumed fishing, and no alignment with Philippine-style publicity. Party leadership consolidation under To Lam keeps foreign policy steady, and the probability of a serious maritime clash is low.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 4 Aug — Tokyo: The 2026 Defense White Paper named China the 'greatest strategic challenge' and, for the first time, framed China, Russia and North Korea as a coordinating bloc.
Through Aug — Senkaku Islands: Armed China Coast Guard vessels sustained a record run of consecutive days in the contiguous zone.
19-20 Aug — Regional: China and Russia amplified rhetorical pushback on the White Paper alongside Wang Yi's Northeast Asia diplomacy.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for a possible upgrade given rising rhetorical intensity. Tokyo accelerates its defense build-up — counter-strike missiles, south-western-island hardening, a higher budget share — and deepens minilateral ties including the Mogami frigate deal with Australia. Expect continued near-daily Senkaku incursions, periodic China-Russia joint air and naval activity near Japanese airspace, and a domestic nuclear-latency debate that Beijing and Moscow will exploit rhetorically. Friction with China over the White Paper language persists but stays diplomatic; a coast-guard incident at the Senkakus is the main escalation risk.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 16-20 Aug — Puncak Jaya, Papua highlands: The TNI conducted repeated drone strikes on a TPNPB headquarters; the group reported structural damage but no fatalities.
17 Aug — Jila district, Mimika, Central Papua: A firefight between the TNI and the Kodap III Puncak group killed one soldier and wounded two.
17-18 Aug — Central Papua: A TNI task force located a TPNPB hideout and killed three members following Independence Day attacks.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The notable shift is the TNI's use of repeated drone strikes against TPNPB in the highlands. Expect a continued cycle of TPNPB ambushes and harassment across Puncak, Intan Jaya, Yahukimo, Nduga and Mimika and expanded TNI operations, driving further civilian displacement and rights complaints; the post-Independence-Day tempo typically eases but does not stop. The Prabowo government prioritises security consolidation and resource projects, which sustain grievances, and there is a risk of a mass-casualty incident — an aircraft downing, hostage-taking, or a strike causing civilian deaths — that internationalises the issue.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: Through Aug — Thai-Cambodia border: The Malaysia-brokered December 2025 ceasefire held but remained fragile, with Cambodia pressing for an urgent Joint Boundary Commission session while Thailand conditioned talks on agreed demarcation mechanisms.
Through Aug — Chanthaburi province: Thai army border-fence construction opposite Battambang drew an ASEAN Observer Team inspection and Cambodian objections.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The ceasefire is likely to hold through the period, sustained by ASEAN monitoring and mutual exhaustion after the July-December 2025 fighting. Main risks are a landmine casualty, a patrol clash near Ta Moan or Ta Krabey or Preah Vihear, or nationalist escalation in either capital. Border demarcation stays deadlocked; expect periodic troop-movement accusations and localised closures rather than renewed large-scale combat.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 5 Aug — New Delhi: Sheikh Hasina addressed a Foreign Correspondents' Club event marking two years since her ouster, angering Dhaka.
23 Aug — Dhaka: PM Tarique Rahman's planned first visit to India was put on hold amid the Hasina-extradition standoff, with bilateral ties described as strained.
Ongoing — Dhaka: July Charter implementation remained deadlocked, with the BNP filing nine of 11 dissent notes over the implementation mechanism and 'source of authority.'
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The BNP government under Tarique Rahman manages a fractious post-transition landscape: Charter-implementation disputes with former allies NCP and Jamaat, Awami League proscription grievances, and economic strain. India relations stay cold over Hasina's continued political activity from Indian soil, and the stalled visit signals a prolonged freeze affecting trade, border, water and transit issues. Risk of political street violence, campus unrest and communal incidents persists; no single flashpoint is likely to breach MODERATE, but cumulative instability is rising.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 6-7 Aug — New Magazine Prison (Colombo) and Kuruwita Prison: Two riots killed three inmates and injured about 23, prompting troop deployments to Welikada and two other jails.
8 Aug — Colombo: A prisoners' rights committee petitioned the UN resident coordinator over deaths and abuses at four facilities.
20-27 Aug — Nationwide: No new significant incident was identified in the window; the situation reflects continuation of the early-August prison unrest.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Prison unrest is likely to recur episodically absent decongestion measures — bail reform, drug-offense sentencing changes, new facilities — given roughly 39,000 inmates against a 10,000 capacity. Expect the NPP government to combine troop deployments and transfers with promises of reform, plus resistance to independent or UN investigations. Broader public order is stable; the risk is a large-scale riot or custodial-death incident that draws sustained international human-rights attention. If calm continues through mid-September, a downgrade toward LOW is defensible.

regions.name: Americas
overview: US hard power is now a fixed feature of the theater: this window alone saw lethal strikes on alleged drug boats on 24 and 25 August (a cumulative roughly 227 killed in about 68 strikes under Operation Southern Spear), two US warships and three Black Hawks arriving at Manta, confirmed US Green Berets operating in Esmeraldas, a pledged $1bn Colombia security package, and a warship group off Venezuela — normalising direct US kinetic involvement and creating multiple flashpoints for an incident near sovereign waters.

Two Andean earthquakes in ten days are straining fiscal space: Peru's magnitude-6.7 Ayacucho quake (20 August, no deaths) followed Colombia's magnitude-7.4 Chocó quake (10 August, toll now around 331 dead and roughly $9.8bn in damage), with Colombia governing under an Article 215 economic-emergency decree and Venezuela's US-backed talks partly pivoting to unfreezing overseas assets for its own quake recovery.

Non-state armed actors are outpacing states at the margins: Haiti's gangs executed a 47-dead massacre and 50-plus mass kidnapping at Kenscoff (23-24 August) and are spreading into five-plus departments during the Kenya-to-multinational handover; Colombia's ELN and FARC dissidents answered the new hardline offensive with drone strikes and a DIJIN police kidnapping; and Peru's and Bolivia's transport sectors are paralysed by extortion rackets and fuel-price shocks respectively.

Elected governments are concentrating executive power and leaning on external patrons and creditors: Fujimori has requested 120-day decree powers, Colombia is under emergency rule, Bolivia's Paz reshuffled his cabinet around an IMF and World Bank package while deploying troops against blockades, and Venezuela's oil revenue sits under US Treasury control — with Bolivia's threatened October national blockades the nearest concrete escalation point.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 15 Aug — Caracas: The interim government confirmed 131 political prisoners released under alternative-measures programs, verified by Foro Penal; the first round of US-brokered government-opposition talks closed on 12 August with a joint statement on judicial reform and recovering frozen overseas funds.

19 Aug — Caracas: Reporting showed the interim government's oil-revenue portal logged only one transaction ($300M) since January, with the US Treasury still holding Venezuelan oil proceeds under Executive Order 14373.
24 Aug — Southern Caribbean: A US military strike on an alleged drug-smuggling vessel killed two, part of the Operation Southern Spear buildup off Venezuela.
25 Aug — Caribbean: A further US strike on an alleged smuggling boat killed four; the cumulative campaign toll reached about 227 killed in roughly 68 strikes.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Both the pressure campaign and the reconciliation track are continuing on their existing trajectory, with no rupture or escalation trigger this week. Expect the September negotiating round to yield further incremental prisoner releases and a nominal judicial and electoral-authority reform package while Delcy Rodríguez consolidates the interim presidency and the Machado camp manoeuvres from outside the process toward a 2026 candidacy and her announced return from exile. US Treasury control of oil revenue and rising US-bound crude volumes will persist; the main escalation risks are a maritime strike close to Venezuelan territorial waters that Caracas frames as an act of war, and a collapse of the talks if the excluded opposition majority rejects the reform terms.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 13-15 Aug — Catatumbo, Norte de Santander: An ELN drone attack killed one soldier and wounded four; drone-dropped explosives later wounded six civilians amid mass forced confinement of communities.

17 Aug — Vía Ocaña-Cúcuta, Norte de Santander: Armed men kidnapped three DIJIN counter-terrorism police; military intelligence attributed the abduction to an ELN front and the Defense Ministry activated a rescue operation.
19 Aug — Bogotá: President de la Espriella's economic-emergency decree took effect (30 days, 15 departments) as the 10 August Chocó earthquake toll rose to about 331 dead and $9.8bn in damage.
26 Aug — El Tambo, Cauca: FARC dissidents attacked the police station with explosive-laden drones; no casualties were reported.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. De la Espriella will press military offensives in Catatumbo, Cauca and the Pacific littoral, backed by the likely partially disbursed US package, while armed groups answer asymmetrically — drone strikes on stations, kidnappings of security personnel, road-infrastructure bombs and forced confinement — producing a steady civilian-harm toll rather than set-piece battles. The economic-emergency decree will face Constitutional Court review, and quake reconstruction competes with security spending for scarce fiscal room. Watch for a high-casualty urban car bomb or a downed aircraft as the escalation markers, and whether reconstruction and tariff-relief negotiations with Washington make the earthquake a rally-round-the-flag event or a governance liability.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 7 Aug — Kenscoff: Viv Ansanm gunmen ambushed a Haitian National Police armored vehicle, injuring three officers and burning the vehicle.
20 Aug — Cap-Haïtien: The first US deportation flight to Haiti since the end of Temporary Protected Status landed with roughly 160-190 deportees; Port-au-Prince airport remained closed to US flights.

23-24 Aug — Kenscoff (Carrefour Maroca): Viv Ansanm gunmen besieged a police station and a church sheltering displaced people, killing at least 47, kidnapping 50-plus and torching 25 homes — one of the largest mass kidnappings in recent Haitian history.

26 Aug — Port-au-Prince: UN and analyst reporting confirmed gang consolidation into Artibonite, Centre and other departments; the Gang Suppression Force announced planned deployments to Cité Soleil and Artibonite.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, worsening. Security will deteriorate further before the Gang Suppression Force reaches operational strength; the Kenscoff hostage crisis may produce either a negotiated release or executions, both of which will further discredit the police and Transitional Presidential Council. Gang territorial expansion into Artibonite and Centre will sever more of the road network and deepen displacement, now above 1.4 million. A credible nationwide 13 December election is now improbable — expect either a narrowed or postponed vote or a legitimacy crisis over the Council's mandate — while low-volume US TPS-end deportation flights continue into a country that cannot absorb returnees.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 2-3 Aug — Nationwide: The seventh total grid collapse of 2026 left blackouts of up to 20 hours a day in Havana and more than 87 hours in Matanzas, followed by cacerolazo protests and arrests.
20 Aug — Washington: The US imposed fresh sanctions on 10 Cuban state-owned mining, metals and construction firms plus ICAP leadership, and broadened curbs on US-person transactions.
~24 Aug — Jaimanitas, Havana: Residents blocked Fifth Avenue with a pot-banging protest over a prolonged blackout and water outage; a vehicle reportedly carrying state agents drove at the crowd.
Through Aug — Nationwide: Prisoners Defenders documented a record 1,327 political prisoners, 36 of them added in July.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. With the grid running roughly 1,000 MW against an approximately 1,800 MW deficit and the US oil blockade allowing only sporadic Russian tankers, further total blackouts are near-certain, each triggering another round of localised cacerolazos and mass arrests that push the political-prisoner count higher. The 20 August sanctions will accelerate foreign-firm withdrawal and worsen fuel and food shortages. The regime's tools remain repression plus emigration as a pressure valve; the low-probability, high-impact scenario to watch is a broad, simultaneous multi-province uprising on the scale of July 2021, most likely triggered by a prolonged nationwide outage during peak heat.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 16-23 Aug — Beijing: President Noboa made an eight-day state visit, meeting Xi Jinping and other leaders to seek the lifting of suspensions on shrimp processors and to secure mining and energy investment.
20 Aug — Manta: The Defense Ministry confirmed the arrival of three US Black Hawk helicopters and two US warships to roughly triple maritime patrol capacity against drug boats.
20 Aug — Washington: The US Treasury sanctioned an Ecuador-to-US cocaine trafficking network and 10 Ecuador-based fishing vessels.

21 Aug — Esmeraldas province: The Defense Ministry confirmed joint operations with US SOUTHCOM against cartels near the Colombian border, with a local official saying US Green Berets are operating in the province.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect the US presence at Manta and in Esmeraldas to become semi-permanent, with more publicised joint interdictions and possible US strikes on vessels off Ecuador's Pacific coast; cartel groups such as Los Choneros and Lobos will likely respond with urban attacks, prison violence and assassinations to signal resilience. Noboa will try to bank Chinese trade and investment concessions without provoking Washington — a balancing act opposition figures and some in the US will keep attacking, alongside criticism of the constitutional 'suspension window.' Homicide rates and port-city violence remain the key metrics, and rights complaints over joint US-Ecuador operations will keep accumulating.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 14-20 Aug — Madre de Dios (Tambopata National Reserve): Navy heliborne operations targeted illegal gold mining that has advanced into the protected reserve, with documented mercury contamination of waterways and Indigenous communities.
~18 Aug — Lima: The Fujimori administration formally requested 120 days of delegated legislative powers covering public security, labor-market flexibility and state modernization.
20 Aug — Ayacucho (near Upahuacho): A magnitude-6.7 earthquake injured at least two and damaged homes, schools and health centers; no fatalities were reported.
25 Aug — Lima / Callao: A 24-hour transport stoppage by 11 unions cut more than 80% of service in protest at extortion and the killing of drivers.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Congress is likely to grant Fujimori delegated powers in narrowed form given her right-wing coalition, enabling a rapid succession of emergency decrees on mining, extortion and labor flexibility that the Senate can later contest — friction but not a standoff. Transport-sector extortion and driver killings will keep producing rolling strikes and localised states of emergency in Lima, Callao and Trujillo, with a militarised policing response of limited effect on the underlying rackets. The Madre de Dios anti-mining campaign will see tactical interdictions but continued frontier expansion of illegal mining and possible violent pushback from miners' federations.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 17 Aug — La Paz: The government issued Decree 5676 raising diesel prices about 84% for large consumers, immediately drawing blockade threats from farm and transport groups.
21 Aug — La Paz: President Paz fired his Economy Minister amid unrest and to smooth congressional approval of an IMF (about $1.9bn) and World Bank financing package and an Investment Law.

26 Aug — Yapacaní and the Trópico de Cochabamba: Military and police deployed to prevent road blockades over the fuel decree, even as the government conceded the decree must be repealed within 48 hours and Morales-aligned organisations met in the Chapare to decide further measures.
Ongoing — Chapare: The Evo Morales arrest warrant issued 29 July remains unenforced; the June state of emergency runs to 20 September.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, trending toward escalation. The Paz government will likely repeal or heavily dilute Decree 5676 within days, but the underlying subsidy-cut agenda tied to the IMF program guarantees recurring fuel shortages and blockade cycles into October. Congressional approval of the IMF arrangement and Investment Law is probable but slow, with the cabinet reshuffle signalling accommodation of legislators. The Chapare standoff persists: the state will not risk an armed operation to detain Morales before the crisis eases, and his movement retains the capacity to paralyse the road network. The highest-risk window is October, when transport and rural federations have threatened coordinated national blockades.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 20-21 Aug — Cap-Haïtien: The first US TPS-end deportees arrived in Haiti as the Dominican Republic continued parallel mass expulsions of roughly 1,000 Haitians a day, with rights groups documenting abusive detention conditions.
20-27 Aug — Nationwide: No discrete security incident on Dominican territory surfaced for the window.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The deportation campaign will almost certainly continue at its current pace through the fall, now compounded by the US ending TPS protections and beginning its own direct deportation flights to Haiti — creating a convergence of Dominican and US removal pressure onto a Haitian state already unable to secure Port-au-Prince. This raises secondary humanitarian and stability risk without materially changing the Dominican Republic's own low direct-conflict profile; watch for any spillover if Haitian gang control reaches the border departments of Centre and Nord-Est, and continued rights-group documentation of batey raid conditions as the main source of reputational rather than security risk.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 6 Aug — Land Settlement, Manchester: A police operation drew gunfire from two men; police returned fire and recovered a shotgun and 50 rounds, with no injuries.

~10 Aug — Spur Tree Hill, Manchester: An off-duty road-rage shootout between two police corporals left one officer grazed, with INDECOM and the police standards unit investigating amid conflicting accounts.
26 Aug — Manchester: One man was killed in a dispute.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Jamaica's pattern of steady, largely operationally-justified police shootings continues, fitting the established profile of targeted suspect confrontations rather than a broadening security crisis. The more notable development is the internal police-on-police shootout under INDECOM investigation in Manchester, which — if it reveals systemic firearms-discipline issues — could draw scrutiny over the coming quarter, but absent escalation this remains the lowest-priority file in the region; peak hurricane season in September is the more material near-term risk to Jamaican stability.
